title: How to Build an IB SEHS Study Group for Fall
summary: Build an effective IB SEHS study group for September-November with clear roles, focused sessions, exam practice, accountability, and IA safeguards.
body_markdown:
An effective **IB SEHS study group** is small, structured, and built around work that every member completes. During September-November, meet consistently, use active recall and exam-style questions, and finish each session with measurable individual outputs.


This approach reflects the demands of Sports, Exercise and Health Science. Students must recall knowledge, apply concepts, interpret data, evaluate experimental procedures, and communicate scientific reasoning across exercise physiology and nutrition, biomechanics, and sports psychology and motor learning.


### Understand what your IB SEHS study group must practise


For the course first assessed in 2026, the official IB subject brief assigns **36%** of the final grade to Paper 1, **40%** to Paper 2, and **24%** to the scientific investigation. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice, data-based, and experimental-work questions. Paper 2 contains short-answer and extended-response questions.


Your group should therefore practise:


- Accurate recall of terminology, processes, and relationships
- Application of knowledge to unfamiliar contexts
- Analysis of data, methods, trends, and limitations
- Concise answers that address IB command terms


The IB does not require study-group participation. Group size, frequency, and roles are recommendations, not official rules. For most students, **3-5 members** provides useful discussion without excessive waiting or coordination.


### Choose members by working habits


Invite students who arrive prepared, attempt questions independently, and accept correction. Members do not need the same predicted grade, but major differences in commitment can make the group ineffective.


Agree on four rules:


1. Meetings begin and end on time.
2. Everyone completes the preparation.
3. Answers are justified using SEHS concepts or evidence.
4. Social conversation waits until the planned work is finished.


Use a two-week trial. If someone repeatedly arrives unprepared, address the problem rather than allowing the group to become an informal social gathering.


### Use a repeatable 75-minute structure


Open-ended meetings often lead to rereading or one confident student doing all the explaining. A fixed agenda makes participation visible.


Time Activity Required output


0-10 minutes Closed-book retrieval quiz Individual answers


10-25 minutes Compare and correct responses Corrections with reasons


25-50 minutes Timed exam-style questions One complete response per student


50-65 minutes Peer marking Mark allocation and improvement note


65-75 minutes Plan the next meeting Assigned topic, questions, and roles


Rotate the roles of **facilitator** , **timekeeper** , and **checker** . The facilitator follows the agenda, the timekeeper protects each section, and the checker verifies answers against a trustworthy source.


Research reviews support retrieval practice as a useful classroom strategy, although it is not automatically better than every alternative. Require each student to answer before discussion. Collaboration should strengthen individual retrieval, not replace it.


### Build a September-November SEHS plan


Your sequence should reflect what your teacher has covered. This framework is practical advice, not an official IB calendar.


Period Main purpose Suggested group tasks


September Establish routines and diagnose gaps Baseline quiz, syllabus map, summaries, short data questions


October Develop application and analysis Mixed questions, graphs, method evaluation, extended responses


November Integrate and test learning Timed paper sections, error analysis, individual reattempts


In September, create a syllabus tracker for the three themes. Mark each subtopic as **not taught** , **developing** , or **secure** . Use[RevisionDojo's SEHS Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-new-syllabus/notes) to clarify concepts, then close the notes before retrieval practice.


In October, move beyond definitions. After reviewing energy systems, for example, explain which systems predominate in different activities and how intensity and duration affect their contribution. The[SEHS Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-new-syllabus/questionbank) provides topic-focused practice.


In November, combine topics and introduce timing. Use unfamiliar athlete scenarios, data sets, and longer responses. RevisionDojo's[guide to earning a 7 in IB SEHS](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-ib-sehs) offers an individual study framework for work between meetings.


### Make every discussion exam-focused


A correct scientific explanation does not automatically earn full marks. Students must follow the command term and provide the required depth.


Use this peer-review sequence:


- Underline the **command term** .
- Identify the SEHS concept being assessed.
- Locate each distinct creditworthy point.
- Check that mechanisms are explained, not merely named.
- Remove repetition and unsupported claims.
- Rewrite the response individually.


Keep a shared count of error categories but separate individual logs. Categories may include **knowledge** , **application** , **data interpretation** , **experimental design** , **command term** , and **timing** . Reattempt errors later without notes to check whether the correction lasted.


### Protect scientific investigation integrity


The current SEHS scientific investigation is an open-ended task in which each student gathers and analyses data to answer a formulated research question. The IB permits limited collaboration in suitable small-group contexts, including some similar methodologies when variables and data meet subject conditions, but the submitted report remains individual.


Members may discuss controls, ethics, graph selection, and sources of uncertainty. They should not write each other's sections, exchange finished paragraphs, or produce near-identical analyses. The IB academic integrity policy requires authentic work and treats collusion that creates an unfair advantage as misconduct.


Ask your teacher what is permitted before sharing investigation files. Students can consult the[RevisionDojo SEHS IA Guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ia-guides/ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-new-syllabus) or use the[SEHS IA Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grader/rubric/sehs-new-ia) , but their decisions, analysis, and wording must remain their own.


### Fix common study-group failures


A group is failing when it produces extensive notes but few attempted questions, one student teaches continuously, marking is overly generous, or nobody revisits mistakes.


Apply these corrections:


- Replace “revise biomechanics” with “complete and mark six force and motion questions.”
- Require silent individual attempts before discussion.
- Limit explanations, then ask another member to restate the reasoning.
- Record the next task list, not other students' completed answers.
- Reattempt selected mistakes at the next meeting.
- Cancel meetings that have no prepared agenda.


The strongest evidence of a productive session is a completed response, corrected misconception, recorded score, or successful reattempt.


### Conclusion


A fall IB SEHS study group works when it combines dependable membership, a fixed agenda, retrieval, exam-style application, and honest feedback. Establish routines in September, strengthen analysis in October, and introduce mixed, timed practice in November.


Keep collaboration focused on explanation and correction while preserving individual responsibility. RevisionDojo's SEHS Study Notes, Questionbank, and IA tools can support this work, but every member should produce and improve their own answers.
